key_insight: CROSS decodes implicit cultural symbols and cross-modal incongruence in memes to detect harmful intent while producing human-interpretable rationales.
problem_solved: Detects meme-based social abuse that relies on subtle cultural references and image-text mismatch, addressing cultural blindness, satire-vs-abuse ambiguity, and opaque model reasoning.
method: Culture-aware symbolic grounding: represent and retrieve cultural/symbolic context tied to visual elements and references.
Cross-modal incongruence detection: identify semantic or affective mismatches between image and text that signal harmful intent.
Interpretable reasoning & boundary modeling: produce explicit rationales and a boundary-aware decision module to distinguish satire from abuse.
impact: Enables more accurate, culturally informed moderation of memes with fewer false positives and transparent, auditable decisions—useful for content-moderation systems and responsible multimodal AI development.
visual_elements: Annotated meme example: image with highlighted symbols and overlaid text showing extracted cultural context and model rationale.
Pipeline flowchart: stages for symbol grounding → cross-modal incongruence detection → rationale generation → final decision.
Satire vs. abuse spectrum: a simple continuum visualization showing boundary-aware classification and uncertainty.
Performance/qualitative panel: side-by-side examples of model explanations vs. baseline (no explanation) to show interpretability gains.
paper_title: They Said Memes Were Harmless-We Found the Ones That Hurt: Decoding Jokes, Symbols, and Cultural References
paper_authors: Sahil Tripathi, Gautam Siddharth Kashyap, Mehwish Nasim, Jian Yang, Jiechao Gao
